I'll read the brief first and follow it exactly until `E3.md` and `E3_DONE` are committed.The brief requires predictions committed before any measurement. I’ll read the REASON records and existing theory notes so those predictions are grounded, then commit them.The records and §7 are enough to freeze the question before any measurement. I’ll commit those predictions and the scoring rules first, then measure only from a script.Predictions are committed. Next I’ll build the tokenizer and the measurement script, and check them against the saved programs before any class counts.The tokenizer matches Qwen’s token ids. Reference rebuilds also need character offsets, so I’ll add those before measuring.The suite enumerator can blow up on a long word class before it has the 64 shortest cases. I'll fix that, then run the measurement.E3 is committed. Class (a) — a total written machine that is not equivalent to its reference — is 54 of 219 R1 failures and 6 of 45 R2 failures, 60 of 264 in all.

On those 60, the shortest distinguishing word is usually length 1. Both the reference suite at the reference's reachable size and the written-table suite at written states + 2 expose every one of them within 64 cases, and 57 of 60 within 16. Equivalent correct calls agreed on every executed suite word.The search for an installed `tokenizers` package was stopped. It was not needed: the E3 measurement used the local Qwen tokenizer files and is already committed.
